chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Our companions differ regarding the voluntary prayer; some of them pray four and forty, and some of them pray fifty. So inform me with which you act, how it is, so that I may act upon the like of it.' He said, 'I pray one and fifty.'

Then he said, 'Hold on!' And he counted with his hand: 'The midday is eight, and four after the Dhuhr, and four before the Asr, and two after the Maghrib, and two before the last Isha, and two after the Isha while seated, accounted as one while standing, and eight for the night prayer, and the Witr is three, and two of the Fajr, and the Obligatory ones are seventeen. So that is one and fifty.'
ai.seo_question: How many voluntary rak'at did Imam al-Rida (AS) perform daily and how were they distributed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi resolves the scholarly variance regarding the quantity of voluntary prayers by providing a precise, comprehensive count of fifty-one rak'at performed by Imam al-Rida (AS). It systematically categorizes these prayers into pre- and post-obligatory units, the night prayer (Tahajjud), and the Witr, offering a practical model for daily devotion. This detailed enumeration underscores the Shia emphasis on balancing ritual consistency with spiritual flexibility in supererogatory acts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws, ‘Our companions are differing regarding the voluntary Salāts. Some of them are praying forty four (Rak’at), and some of them are praying fifty (Rak’at). So inform me with which are youasws acting upon, how it is so that I can act upon the like of it’. So heasws said: ‘Iasws pray fifty-one Rak’at’.

Then heasws said: ‘Hold on!’ And heasws counted by hisasws hand – ‘The midday is eight (Rak’at), and four after Al-Zohr, and four before Al-Asr, and two Rak’at after Al-Maghrib, and two Rak’at before Isha the last, and two Rak’at after Al-Isha while seated, accounted as one Rak’at while standing, and eight for the night Salāt, and Al-Witr is of three, and two Rak’at of Al-Faj, and the Obligatory ones are seventeen. So that is fifty-one (Rak’at)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that our people have differences about optional Salah (prayer). Certain ones among them say it is forty-four and others perform fifty. Please tell me about what you perform and how is it, so I can do similarly. He (the Imam) said, ‘I perform fifty-one Rak‘at.’

He (the Imam) then said, ‘Hold on to it.’ He (the Imam) counted with his hand saying, ‘Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) is eight. There are four after al-Dhuhr, four before al-‘Asr, two after al-Maghrib, two before al-‘Isha’, two after al-‘Isha’ in a sitting position which are counted as one Rak‘at in a standing position. There are eight Rak‘at of nightly Salah (prayer), three of al-witr and two at dawn. Obligatory Salah (prayer) is seventeen Rak‘at and this becomes fifty-one Rak‘at.’”
